subject: obstetrics-gynaecology
title: Postpartum Haemorrhage, the 4 Ts and First-Line Uterotonics

steps.tx: Blood loss over five hundred millilitres after vaginal birth or a litre after caesarean is **postpartum haemorrhage**. Visual estimation understates loss by half, so weighed drapes and shock index guide resuscitation. It remains the worlds leading direct cause of maternal death. Careful history taking and examination help place this finding in the right clinical context before treatment is planned.
steps.say: Postpartum haemorrhage exceeds five hundred millilitres vaginally and visual estimation understates it.

steps.tx: Failure of the uterus to contract, responsible for seventy percent of cases, is **atonic PPH**. Overdistension, prolonged labour, chorioamnionitis and retained tissue all exhaust the muscle. A soft boggy uterus rising in the abdomen is the finding. Correlating this finding with imaging and laboratory results prevents both delayed treatment and unnecessary intervention in most patients.
steps.say: Atonic PPH from a soft boggy uterus causes seventy percent of postpartum haemorrhage.

steps.tx: Sorting every haemorrhage into tone, tissue, trauma and thrombin is the **4 Ts** framework. Each category has a distinct first treatment, from uterotonics to repair to transfusion. Teams call out the likely T while resuscitation runs. Early recognition matters because timely treatment gives clearly better outcomes than waiting for complications to develop first.
steps.say: The 4 Ts sort haemorrhage into tone, tissue, trauma and thrombin with distinct treatments.

steps.tx: The first line uterotonic contracting the uterus within minutes is **oxytocin**. Slow intravenous bolus followed by infusion is the standard sequence. Rapid bolus drops blood pressure and is avoided in cardiac disease. Students should connect this fact with the presenting symptoms, since examination questions usually test that clinical link directly.
steps.say: Oxytocin is the first line uterotonic by slow bolus then infusion.

steps.tx: The prostaglandin F2 alpha injection for refractory atony is **carboprost**. Given intramuscularly or into the myometrium, it rescues many oxytocin failures. Asthma forbids it because it bronchoconstricts powerfully. Documenting this finding clearly in the notes guides the next clinician and supports safe, well planned further management.
steps.say: Carboprost rescues refractory atony but is forbidden in asthma for bronchoconstriction.

steps.tx: The ergot alkaloid giving sustained tetanic uterine contraction is **methylergometrine**. Hypertension and cardiac disease forbid it because it vasoconstricts equally powerfully. It is given intramuscularly, never as a rapid intravenous push. When this picture is seen in practice, urgent senior review is wise whenever there is any doubt about severity.
steps.say: Methylergometrine gives sustained contraction but hypertension forbids it.

steps.tx: Calling for help, rubbing the uterus and emptying the bladder open every response, the **first response bundle**. A full bladder mechanically prevents contraction and is drained immediately. Two large bore cannulae and blood samples follow within minutes. Understanding this mechanism explains the symptoms, the investigation findings and the logic behind each step of treatment given.
steps.say: The first response bundle rubs the uterus, empties the bladder and gains access.

steps.tx: Shock index, heart rate divided by systolic pressure, flags hidden severity as the **shock index**. Values at or above one predict transfusion need better than blood pressure alone. It costs nothing and trends beautifully. This distinction changes management, so it should be settled early rather than after empirical treatment has already begun.
steps.say: Shock index at or above one predicts transfusion need better than pressure alone.

steps.tx: Simultaneous resuscitation and cause treatment, never sequential, is the governing **parallel principle**. One team member owns uterotonics, another access and blood, another documentation and timings. Role allocation is rehearsed in drills. Careful history taking and examination help place this finding in the right clinical context before treatment is planned.
steps.say: Parallel resuscitation and cause treatment with allocated roles governs haemorrhage response.
